newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong's future chief greets Chinese leaders.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's future chief greets Chinese leaders.

text.p: Senior Chinese leaders on Wednesday welcomed Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa to Beijing for a visit keenly watched by the territory's residents for hints on how he plans to rule.
Foreign Minister Qian Qichen greeted Tung, who will lead the British colony after it returns to Chinese rule on July 1 next year, at the Diaoyutai state guesthouse in western Beijing.

Both Qian and Tung declined to answer questions on the substance of the visit by the shipping tycoon who will become Hong Kong's first Chinese chief executive after a century and a half of British colonial rule.
Many Hong Kong residents are eager to know more about Tung's plans for his first post-colonial adminstration and to learn whether current senior civil servants will keep their jobs.
Later on Wednesday, Tung was scheduled to meet Premier Li Peng, who formally appointed him as Hong Kong chief executive-designate on Monday, and President Jiang Zemin.
It was Jiang who signalled in January that Tung was China's favourite for chief executive when he singled out the tycoon for a warm, personal handshake at a reception in Beijing.
The 59-year-old wealthy businessman was chosen last week by a 400-member, Beijing-controlled Selection Committee.
One of Tung's first tasks in the twilight of British rule will be to put together an advisory cabinet called the Executive Council and to decide which senior civil servants to keep.
While much Hong Kong speculation has focused on his intentions for current senior administrators, China said on Tuesday that it would make the final decision on recruitment of senior civil servants.

"For senior officials, they need the nomination of the top administrative official and to finally obtain appointment by the central government," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang said at a news briefing.
